reason: Irregularly cut margins or tips of sepals, bracts and scales are what FLOPO:0991115 lacerate defines ('margin being irregularly cut, as if torn'); PATO_0001978 cut means regularly divided.
'Bark non-corky' / 'non subéreuse' negates FLOPO:0991126 corky (synonym suberose).
'Nervures peu marquées' = veins, network or lobes not clearly visible; same reading as 'obscure' and 'indistinct' in the previous review.

label: calcarate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a spur, a slender hollow or solid projection, usually from its base. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991029 horned and FLOPO:0991028 beaked. Not PATO:0002540 spur shaped, which is the shape of the spur itself; PO has only petal spur and corolla spur, so presence of a part cannot cover bracts, leaf bases and anther thecae.
reason: A well-defined botanical term (bearing a spur) used on bracts, leaf bases, sepals and anther thecae; no PATO or FLOPO term and no general PO spur class.
A semi-superior ovary is the same position as a half-inferior one (lower part fused to the receptacle, upper part free); add as a synonym of FLOPO:0991133.
Crest-shaped wings, callus or anther appendages are raised, irregular ridges, as in FLOPO:0991196 crested; strictly the part is a crest rather than bearing one, so the match is weak.
'Sub-' + emarginate is the approximate-value pattern, as for 'suborbicular'; PATO_0002234 emarginate exists.
A vague likeness to a flap on unlike parts (callus, papillae, aril tongues); it does not name a definite shape.
Confluence is relational (PATO_0002512 confluent with): 'not confluent into a marginal vein', 'in the sinuses'; the relation without its second term is rejected, like 'contiguous'.
Opalescent (opalin) drupes are milky and translucent; PATO translucent captures the firm part, and the play of colour is too rare (2 floras) to justify a new class.
A growing-season or ecological group of grasses (often C4), not a quality of the plant's form.
A slit-shaped ostiole is a narrow, elongate opening: PATO_0002482 slit-like.
Bicucullate petals or corolla lobes are hooded in two places; FLOPO:0991119 cucullate keeps the hood shape, and the 'two' is lost because no hood part exists to count.

label: tricolporate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a pollen grain by virtue of its having three compound apertures, each a longitudinal furrow (colpus) with a pore at its middle.
reason: A standard palynological character with no PATO or FLOPO term, and PO has no pollen aperture to count.
A spelling variant of salverform (synonyms hypocrateriform, salver-shaped).
Negates FLOPO:0991137 heterostylous.
An S-bend in the filament is S-shaped: PATO_0001878 sigmoid (EXACT synonym S-shaped).
A pseudo-racemose inflorescence looks like a raceme without being one, which is FLOPO:0991197 raceme-like (racemiform).

target: new: colour of a marking (punctate PATO_0001512, dots black PATO_0000317)
reason: Two values joined: the surface is punctate and the dots are black. The colour belongs to the dots, not the bearer, so it is neither a single term nor a continuum.

A comparison with the fertile florets; 'similar' without its second term was rejected in the previous review.
Awl-like = awl-shaped, an EXACT synonym of PATO_0001954 subulate.

Engraved veins are cut into the surface, the same reading as 'impressed', which maps to PATO_0002416 sunken.
A vague count of rays (arms of stellate hairs, umbel rays), like 'few-flowered'; count pattern.
Paniculate inflorescence = FLOPO:0991198 panicle-like (paniculiform); 'narrowly' only qualifies its outline and is dropped.
Negates FLOPO:0991148 crisped (crispate). On hairs it means the hairs are straight, not curled.
Negates FLOPO:0991154 jointed (articulate), the usual character of pedicels.
